{{nihongo|'''Kanasana Shrine'''|Kanasana Jinja|金鑚神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Kamikawa, Saitama|arz|بلده كاميكاوا, اليابان|ceb|Kamikawa-machi (subdistrito sa Hapon)|de|Kamikawa (Saitama)|es|Kamikawa (Saitama)|fa|کامیکاوا، سایتاما|fr|Kamikawa (Saitama)|id|Kamikawa, Saitama|it|Kamikawa (Saitama)|ja|神川町|ko|가미카와정 (사이타마현)|ms|Kamikawa, Saitama|my|ခမိခါဝါမြို့၊ ဆိုင်းတမ|pl|Kamikawa (Saitama)|ru|Камикава (Сайтама)|sv|Kamikawa, Saitama|tl|Kamikawa, Saitama|tr|Kamikawa, Saitama|uk|Камікава (Сайтама)|ur|کامیکاوا، سائیتاما|zh|神川町|qid=Q1346757|lt=Kamikawa, Saitama}}.<ref name="nipponcom-2018a">{{Cite web |date=2018-07-08 |title=Keeping Ancient Mountain Worship Alive at Saitama's Kanasana Shrine |url=https://www.nippon.com/en/guide-to-japan/gu009002/keeping-ancient-mountain-worship-alive-at-saitama%E2%80%99s-kanasana-shrine.html |access-date=2023-10-25 |website=nippon.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="www2kokugakuinacjp-2023a" /><ref name="ponsonbyfane-2016a">{{Cite book |last=Ponsonby-Fane |first=R. A. B. |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2016-05-dd |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-138-98322-9 |edition=1st |pages=383 |language=English}}</ref> The shrine worships [[Amaterasu]] alongside [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]].

It is a mid-range Ranked Imperial shrine ([[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kanpei-chūsha]]),<ref name="ponsonbyfane-2016a" /> and is a [[:en:Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]] of {{ill|Musashi Province|ar|محافظة موساشي|ca|Província de Musashi|ckb|پارێزگای موساشی|cs|Provincie Musaši|de|Provinz Musashi|eo|Provinco Musaŝi|es|Provincia de Musashi|fa|ولایت موساشی|fr|Province de Musashi|gl|Provincia de Musashi|hak|Musashi-koet|id|Provinsi Musashi|it|Musashi (provincia)|ja|武蔵国|ko|무사시국|lt|Musašio žemė|nl|Musashi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Musashi|pt|Província de Musashi|ru|Мусаси (провинция)|simple|Musashi Province|sk|Musaši (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мусаши|th|แคว้นมูซาชิ|tr|Musashi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Мусаші|vi|Musashi (tỉnh)|zh|武藏國|zh_min_nan|Musasi-kok|zh_yue|武藏國|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province}}, or a second Rank shrine in the province after the [[Ichinomiya]], and is commonly called "Ninomiya-sama".<ref name="www2kokugakuinacjp-2023a" /> It is considered a prestigious shrines in the {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|qid=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}}.<ref name="chocotabi-saitama-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Kanasana Shrine｜CHOCOTABI SAITAMA |url=https://en.chocotabi-saitama.com/spot/34609 |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=CHOCOTABI SAITAMA |language=ja}}</ref> The shrine is believed to have been founded when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} hid the tools of fire in {{ill|Mount Ōmuro (Mount Fuji)|ceb|Ōmuro-yama (bukid sa Hapon)|fa|کوه اومورو (کوه فوجی)|ja|大室山 (富士山)|qid=Q11434369|lt=Mount Ōmuro}}.<ref name="chocotabi-saitama-2023a" /> Every November 23 it hosts a {{Nihongo|firestone festival|火金鑚祭|Hikiri Shinji}}<ref name="www2kokugakuinacjp-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Glossary of Shinto Names and Terms: K |url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/glossary/def_K.html |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref>

== Overview ==
Kanasana Shrine is in {{ill|Kamikawa, Saitama|arz|بلده كاميكاوا, اليابان|ceb|Kamikawa-machi (subdistrito sa Hapon)|de|Kamikawa (Saitama)|es|Kamikawa (Saitama)|fa|کامیکاوا، سایتاما|fr|Kamikawa (Saitama)|id|Kamikawa, Saitama|it|Kamikawa (Saitama)|ja|神川町|ko|가미카와정 (사이타마현)|ms|Kamikawa, Saitama|my|ခမိခါဝါမြို့၊ ဆိုင်းတမ|pl|Kamikawa (Saitama)|ru|Камикава (Сайтама)|sv|Kamikawa, Saitama|tl|Kamikawa, Saitama|tr|Kamikawa, Saitama|uk|Камікава (Сайтама)|ur|کامیکاوا، سائیتاما|zh|神川町|qid=Q1346757|lt=Kamikawa}}, in the northwest of Saitama Prefecture, at an elevation of 343 meters at the base of Mount Mitake. The shrine overlooks the Kannagawa river, which demarcates the border between {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|qid=Q128186|lt=Saitama}} and {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Gunma|af|Gunma-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Gunma|ar|غونما (محافظة)|arz|محافظه جونما|az|Qunma prefekturası|azb|قونما اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Gunma|bat_smg|Gunmas prefektūra|be|Гуму|bg|Гунма|bn|গুন্‌মা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Gunma|cdo|Gunma-gâing|ce|Гумма (префектура)|ceb|Gunma-ken|ckb|پارێزگای گونما|cs|Prefektura Gunma|cy|Gunma (talaith)|da|Gunma-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Gunma|eo|Gubernio Gunma|es|Prefectura de Gunma|et|Gumma prefektuur|eu|Gunma (prefektura)|fa|استان گونما|fi|Gunman prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Gunma|frr|Gunma (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Gunma|gl|Prefectura de Gunma|hak|Gunma-yen|he|גונמה (מחוז)|hr|Gunma (prefektura)|hu|Gunma prefektúra|hy|Գումմա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Gunma|ilo|Prepektura ti Gunma|it|Prefettura di Gunma|ja|群馬県|jv|Préfèktur Gunma|ka|გუმის პრეფექტურა|km|ហ្គឺនម៉ា(ខេត្ត)|kn|ಗನ್ಮ (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|군마현|lt|Gunmos prefektūra|lv|Gummas prefektūra|mk|Гунма (префектура)|mni|ꯒꯨꯟꯃꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|गुन्मा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Gunma|ne|गुन्मा|nl|Gunma (prefectuur)|no|Gunma (prefektur)|nov|Gunma Prefekture|os|Гумма (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Gunma|pl|Prefektura Gunma|pnb|ضلع گنما|pt|Gunma|ro|Prefectura Gunma|ru|Гумма (префектура)|sd|گونما پريفيڪچر|se|Gunma prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Gunma|si|ගුන්මා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Gunma Prefecture|sk|Gunma (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Гунма|su|Préféktur Gunma|sv|Gunma prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Gunma|tg|Префектураи Гумма|th|จังหวัดกุมมะ|tl|Prepektura ng Gunma|tr|Gunma|tt|Гумма (префектура)|uk|Префектура Ґумма|ur|گونما پریفیکچر|vi|Gunma|war|Gunma (prefektura)|wuu|群马县|zh|群馬縣|zh_classical|群馬縣|zh_min_nan|Gunma-koān|zh_yue|群馬縣|qid=Q129499|lt=Gunma prefectures}}. According to legend, following his achievements in the eastern regions, Prince {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} placed a ''hikirigane'' (a metal instrument used for kindling fire) here as a tribute to the revered deities, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]] and [[Amaterasu]].<ref name="nipponcom-2018a" />

== Etymology ==
The name "Kanasana" originates from the term for "iron sand," highlighting the high-quality {{ill|Ironsand|de|Eisensand|es|Arena ferrífera|id|Pasir besi|ja|砂鉄|pt|Areia ferrífera|uk|Залізний пісок|uz|Temir qum|qid=Q1394005|lt=iron sand}} from the Kannagawa River used in traditional sword making. Mount Mitake is steeped in mythology, with legends indicating the presence of iron and copper deposits. Archaeological evidence suggests human settlement in the area dating back between 15,000 and 20,000 years (to the [[:en:Jomon period|Jomon period]], likely for metal mining.<ref name="nipponcom-2018a" />

== Architecture ==
The shrine has a large [[shinboku]] {{ill|Camphor|ar|كافور (مركب كيميائي)|as|কৰ্পূৰ|ast|Alcanfor|azb|کافور|bg|Камфор|bn|কর্পূর|ca|Càmfora|cs|Kafr|da|Kamfer|de|Campher|dv|ކާފޫރު|el|Καμφορά|eo|Kamforo|es|Alcanfor|eu|Kanfor|fa|کافور|fi|Kamferi|fr|Camphre|ga|Camfar|gl|Alcanfor|gu|કપૂર|he|קמפור|hr|Kamfor|hu|Kámfor|hy|Կամֆորա|id|Kapur barus|io|Kamforo|it|Canfora|ja|樟脳|jv|Kapur barus|kcg|A̱bwuncyui|kk|Камфора|kn|ಕರ್ಪೂರ|ko|장뇌|ky|Камфора|la|Camphora|lt|Kamparas|lv|Kampars|mai|कपुर|ml|കർപ്പൂരം (സുഗന്ധദ്രവ്യം)|mr|कापूर|ms|Kapur barus|ne|कपुर|nl|Kamfer|nn|Kamfer|no|Kamfer|pl|Kamfora|pnb|کافور|pt|Cânfora|ro|Camfor|ru|Камфора|sa|कर्पूरम्|sd|ڪافور|sh|Kamfor|simple|Camphor|sk|Gáfor|sl|Kafra|sq|Qafuri|sr|Камфор|su|Kamper|sv|Kamfer|ta|கற்பூரம்|te|కర్పూరం|th|การบูร|tl|Alkampor|tr|Kâfur|ug|كافۇر|uk|Камфора|ur|کافور|uz|Kamfora|vi|Long não|wuu|樟脑|zh|樟腦|zh_yue|樟腦|qid=Q181559|lt=Camphor}} tree, and includes a [[Tahōtō|tahōtō pagoda]] dated from 1534<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-07-08 |title=Keeping Ancient Mountain Worship Alive at Saitama's Kanasana Shrine |url=https://www.nippon.com/en/guide-to-japan/gu009002/keeping-ancient-mountain-worship-alive-at-saitama%E2%80%99s-kanasana-shrine.html |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=nippon.com |language=en}}</ref>

The shrine omits a [[Honden]] (main hall) as the mountain behind it is considered the shrine's [[Shintai]].<ref name="chocotabi-saitama-2023a" /><ref name="www2kokugakuinacjp-2023a" /> It is one of only three major shrines that continue the practice of direct [[:en:Mountain Worship|Mountain Worship]] via [[Kannabi]] alongside {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|qid=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}} and [[Suwa-taisha]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/5/monograph/book/21618 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=2012 |publisher=University of Hawai'i Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |location=Honolulu |pages=195}}</ref><ref name="nipponcom-2018a" /> In this case the [[Kannabi]] is Mimurogatake, a visible peak of Mount Mitake from the shrine's worship hall.<ref name="nipponcom-2018a" />[[File:Kanasana Jinjya Tahōtō 2009.jpg|thumb|Tahoto]]
[[File:Mitake no Kagamiiwa Slickenside rock surface.jpg|thumb|Mitake no Kagami Iwa]]

Above the shrine is an expansive {{ill|Slickenside|af|Wryfkras|cs|Tektonické zrcadlo|de|Harnisch (Geologie)|ko|단층마찰면|nn|Slickenside|pl|Lustro tektoniczne|sk|Tektonické zrkadlo|uk|Дзеркало ковзання|zh|擦痕面|qid=Q478099|lt=slickenslide}}, a smooth rock surface spanning 9 meters with a 4-meter height, showcases a mirrored finish. Scientists attribute its sheen to the intense friction resulting from the Hachiōji tectonic line's emergence around 100 million years ago. Recognized for its geological significance, this rock was designated a national special natural monument in 1956.<ref name="nipponcom-2018a" />
